comments.body:
To add a quick note. The error message here doesn't indicate it, but this is caused by HLSL's overload resolution changes. In C++ the implicit conversion sequence for an explicitly-typed enumeration that is not an enum class is the same as a non-typed enumeration (i.e. it can implicitly convert to int). In `SemaHLSL.cpp` under `CanConvert` we don't properly handle explicitly-typed non-class enumerations.

While this is a bug that we could fix in HLSL without a language change, I've also tagged this as hlsl-next because we do have plans for HLSL 202x to adopt C++ overload resolution rules in order to support global operator overloading and `const` instance methods. That would fix this in the next language version.

labels.name: hlsl-next
labels.description: Bugs for consideration on next language version

title: Error in implicit conversions when enums are involved
